text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said its milling and baking division should record full year earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) for 1996/97 (July-June) near the 1995/96 result.
The division recorded an EBIT of A$30.4 million for the half year to December 31, 1996, down 28.1 percent on the previous corresonding half.
"We will have a much, much stronger second half than first," Goodman Fielder chief executive David Hearn told a media briefing.
Wheat input prices were significantly lower for the second half, although selling prices would also fall, Hearn said.
"Where we net out is going to be a function of trade-offs in those two areas," he said.
"I think we will see profits in that business that will be somewhere near last year's numbers."
Goodman Fielder recorded an EBIT of A$81.1 million in its milling and baking division in 1995/96.
